newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds up on German data, positive outlook.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds up on German data, positive outlook.

text.p: Danish bond prices rose on Thursday, buoyed by lower than expected German April inflation data, with dealers predicting that the positive market mood would continue up to the close provided Germany holds up.
The Danish stock exchange is closed on Friday for the Great Prayer national holiday, opening again Monday morning.
"Prices could well continue rising as long as the German market holds up," one dealer said.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was 0.22 point up from Wednesday's close at 109.74 or 0.15 up from the start yielding 6.51 percent in turnover of 1.7 billion crowns.
The 2006 June future was untraded at 109.06. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.48 point to 88.08.
The crown traded at 3.8091 per mark at 1115 gmt, marginally up from around 3.8095 at the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany was unchanged at 70 points.
The Central Bank was active on the market selling a total of some 200 million crowns worth of seven percent 2007 and five percent 2005 state bonds as part of its routine financing operations.
